A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReTimeCausal and share identifiable methods and experiments despite the title change. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1.pdf ends with references despite referring to appendices; v2.pdf includes readable Appendices A–L.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original causal-discovery experiments on synthetic time series and a CausalRivers subgraph.

after.justification: Tables 1–3 retain original experiments, while Appendix I adds benchmark evaluations, ablations, sensitivity tests and convergence observations.

M1.justification: The stated kernel regression model changes substantively: v1 Equations 3 and 5 predict kernel features phi(X) using p-by-p matrices, whereas v2 Equations 4 and 6 predict completed original variables from lagged kernel features using p-by-d matrices. This revises the prediction target and regression objective. The surrounding EM loop, noise injection, smoothing and pruning remain.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic linear/nonlinear series and CausalRivers. V2 retains this coverage and adds NetSim simulated fMRI connectivity data and the Medical and PM25 domains of CausalTime (Appendix I.5, Tables 9–10), substantially broadening the evaluated domains.

E2.justification: Rhino+TimeMixer and AERCA+TimeMixer are newly evaluated in all three main comparison tables. The original PCMCI+TimeMixer, PCMCI+EM, DYNOTEARS variants with TimeMixer, and CUTS+ remain. These additions substantially expand the comparator set beyond the original four alternatives.

E3.justification: V2 adds SID evaluation to Tables 2–3 and SHD to the formerly F1-only CausalRivers comparison. New experiments introduce controlled sortability conditions, hyperparameter sweeps, and lag-order evaluations using temporally unrolled graphs with CUTS+ summary graphs shared across lags. These are additional evaluation designs; newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish changes to retained experimental procedures.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's missingness and graph-size comparisons, Appendix I adds a noise-injection ablation, controlled nonlinear-function and lag-order comparisons, sortability robustness tests, pruning visualizations, joint imputation/discovery trajectories, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis. These directly investigate component necessity, optimization behavior and robustness that v1 did not experimentally isolate.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly reports averages over multiple runs with standard-error bands. Both versions already provide mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for CausalRivers and suppress deviations in most other tables. Explicit run counts and seeds remain unspecified; the PDFs do not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: The original ReTimeCausal synthetic F1 and SHD entries are retained, but other results change. Table 2 revises PCMCI+EM's 50-variable SHD/F1 from 138/0.258 to 124/0.311. Table 3 revises ReTimeCausal's reported CausalRivers F1 at 20%/60% missingness from 0.471/0.436 to 0.463/0.414. V2 also adds baseline scores, metric entries and extensive appendix results, including CUTS+ outperforming ReTimeCausal on Medical at 20% missingness (0.667 versus 0.658).

T1.justification: V1 states asymptotic consistency but supplies no referenced appendix proof. V2 adds a conditional proof of Proposition 4.1, a finite-sample/finite-iteration SHD bound in Theorem G.1, and computational complexity derivations. It also corrects the summary-graph definition, replaces invariant structural functions with invariant causal directions, adds faithfulness, and specifies additional regularity, tuning and local-convergence conditions.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's existing asymptotic-consistency claim, v2 explicitly claims guarantees in both idealized and realistic settings as a main contribution. The abstract drops the physics-guided imputation and cross-frequency-resolution characterization and centers the contribution on consistency between imputation and structure recovery. Joint EM/ANM learning and empirical advantage remain central.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits the consistency result to an idealized estimator and explains that approximate back-projection and feature sparsity do not guarantee variable-level recovery. It clarifies the discrete-grid treatment of irregular observations and adds limitations concerning instantaneous effects, changing causal graphs and computation. Section 5.3 now acknowledges modest CausalRivers accuracy and competitors' better SHD or SID, replacing v1's broadly positive interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 supplies pseudocode, model-specific pruning procedures, three-layer imputation-network details, RFF implementation information, and dataset/method hyperparameters in Table 12. It also identifies the RTX 4090 hardware and baseline repository links. V1 provided mostly generic descriptions and unresolved appendix references. These are substantial new disclosures, without establishing that all corresponding settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against continuous-time Neural Graphical Modeling and entropy-based summary-graph discovery, distinguishing discrete lag recovery and theoretical guarantees. V2 also incorporates Rhino, AERCA, CausalTime, sortability research and additional EM/kernel estimation theory. Existing related-work material is partly relocated rather than removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, motivation, problem setup and method explanations are extensively rewritten, especially the separation of neural imputation from kernel-based graph estimation. Related work is reorganized between Section 2 and Appendix A, and organized supporting sections replace dangling appendix references. The title, author information and inconsistent ReCausalTime naming also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Tables 1–3 gain comparator rows and redesigned metric groupings, while Figures 1–2 receive revised graphics, legends and placement. V2 adds pruning heatmaps, a convergence plot with uncertainty shading, algorithm pseudocode, and notation, ablation, benchmark and hyperparameter tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses substantial weaknesses in the supplied v1: missing referenced proofs and algorithm descriptions, sparse implementation information, and little direct evidence for key design choices. Conditional theoretical arguments, reproducibility details, targeted ablations and broader comparisons make the work substantially easier to assess. Explicit qualifications and acknowledgment of unfavorable metrics improve the interpretation of results. The practical pipeline still lacks an unconditional recovery guarantee, and run counts remain unspecified, but these residual limitations do not outweigh the gains.
